paper_title: Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells Enabled by a Sequentially Deposited Bilayer Structure

qa_pairs.question: What is the maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) achieved by the opaque organic solar cell based on the PTB7-Th/IEICO-4F bilayer structure?
qa_pairs.answer: The opaque PTB7-Th/IEICO-4F bilayer device achieved a maximum PCE of 12.0% with a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 25.4 mA/cm² when processed with 2% 1-chloronaphthalene (CN) as an additive.
qa_pairs.source_title: Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells Enabled by a Sequentially Deposited Bilayer Structure

qa_pairs.question: How does the sequential deposition of the donor and acceptor layers influence the internal junction physics of the PTB7-Th/IEICO-4F device?
qa_pairs.answer: Sequential deposition allows for the enrichment of the donor and acceptor at their respective interfaces, leading to the formation of a p-i-n-like junction. This specific architecture facilitates more efficient charge carrier transportation and extraction compared to standard mixtures.
qa_pairs.source_title: Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells Enabled by a Sequentially Deposited Bilayer Structure

qa_pairs.question: What solvent strategy was employed to ensure the PTB7-Th donor layer remained intact during the deposition of the acceptor layer?
qa_pairs.answer: A semi-orthogonal solvent system was used, specifically adding n-butanol to o-xylene in a 3:1 volume ratio for the acceptor solution. Because PTB7-Th has poor solubility in n-butanol, this mixture prevents the donor film from being washed off during sequential deposition.
qa_pairs.source_title: Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells Enabled by a Sequentially Deposited Bilayer Structure

qa_pairs.question: Why is the bilayer structure more effective than the bulk heterojunction (BHJ) structure for maintaining high average visible light transmittance (AVT) in semitransparent cells?
qa_pairs.answer: In BHJ structures, increasing the active layer thickness to improve efficiency unavoidably enhances the donor (PTB7-Th) absorption in the visible region, reducing AVT. In a bilayer structure, the thickness of the IEICO-4F acceptor can be increased (from 50 to 70 nm) to boost efficiency because IEICO-4F has strong near-infrared absorption but relatively weak visible light absorption, thereby preserving high AVT.
qa_pairs.source_title: Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells Enabled by a Sequentially Deposited Bilayer Structure

qa_pairs.question: How does the addition of 2% 1-chloronaphthalene (CN) affect the recombination mechanisms and exciton dissociation in PTB7-Th/IEICO-4F bilayer devices?
qa_pairs.answer: The addition of 2% CN reduces both bimolecular and trap-assisted recombination, as shown by the decrease in the Voc vs. light intensity slope from 1.39 kT/q to 1.27 kT/q. Furthermore, it increases the exciton dissociation probability from 90.18% to 92.35% by inhibiting the aggregation of IEICO-4F and increasing the donor-acceptor interface area.
qa_pairs.source_title: Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells Enabled by a Sequentially Deposited Bilayer Structure

qa_pairs.question: Compare the performance of the best bilayer semitransparent organic solar cell (ST-OSC) with the best BHJ-structured ST-OSC reported in this study.
qa_pairs.answer: The best bilayer-structured ST-OSC outperformed the BHJ-structured device, achieving a PCE of 8.5% and an AVT of 21.5%, compared to the BHJ device's PCE of 8.1% and AVT of 21.1%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells Enabled by a Sequentially Deposited Bilayer Structure

qa_pairs.question: What are the color characteristics of the semitransparent devices as evaluated by the CIE 1931 chromaticity diagram?
qa_pairs.answer: The best semitransparent devices (A-D) exhibit color coordinates near (0.26, 0.30) with correlated color temperatures (CCT) ranging from 10,764 K to 11,310 K.
qa_pairs.source_title: Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells Enabled by a Sequentially Deposited Bilayer Structure

qa_pairs.question: What is the configuration of the transparent top electrode used to replace the standard 100 nm Ag electrode in semitransparent devices?
qa_pairs.answer: The semitransparent devices utilized a transparent top electrode composed of 1 nm of Gold (Au) and 12 nm of Silver (Ag).
qa_pairs.source_title: Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells Enabled by a Sequentially Deposited Bilayer Structure
